History and Physical (H&P – Super Detailed)

Consult Summary:
32-year-old woman with 3-day history of profuse diarrhoea, vomiting, feverishness and periumbilical abdominal pain, likely infectious gastroenteritis; advised ongoing oral re-hydration, simple diet, urgent clinic review for stool culture and hydration check, with A&E escalation if deterioration.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Diarrhoea, vomiting, subjective fever, abdominal pain.  
• Onset & timeline: Began 3 days ago; persistent and not improving.  
   – Day 1: Watery stools progressing to very loose stools.  
   – Day 3 (today): ≥4 bowel motions already; continues to vomit liquids/food, last emesis 2 h prior to consult after breakfast.  
• Character of diarrhoea: Initially watery, now very loose; frequency high (“lost count,” ≥4 today). No blood.  
• Vomiting: Unable to retain water, tea or other liquids.  
• Fever: Feels “literally boiling”; no thermometer reading available.  
• Abdominal pain: Periumbilical, sore to touch, colicky, coincides with urge to defecate.  
• Urination: Passing urine; last void ~1 h before consult; colour not observed; denies haematuria.  
• Associated symptoms: No rash.  
• Exposures: Brother with similar illness; reports school outbreak. No recent travel.  
• Aggravating/relieving factors: Not stated.  
• Self-care: Oral rehydration salt (salt–sugar mix) solution 3×/day for past 2 days; no benefit due to ongoing vomiting.  
• Review of systems (pertinent negatives): No prior bowel habit disturbance; no chronic constipation/diarrhoea; no previous abdominal pain other than menstrual cramps; no rectal bleeding.

Past Medical History:
• Generally healthy.  
• Dysmenorrhoea (occasional menstrual cramps).  
• Surgical history: None.  
• Past abdominal problems: None.

Medications:
• Vitamin D (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
• Ibuprofen as needed for menstrual cramps (dose/route/frequency not documented).

Allergies:
• Not documented (missing).

Social History:
• Occupation: Graphic designer; working from home today due to illness.  
• Lives with mother and brother (brother currently symptomatic).  
• Tobacco: Never smoker.  
• Alcohol: “A pint from time to time.”  
• Recreational drugs: Denies use.

Family History:
• Brother: Similar gastro-intestinal symptoms x few days (possible contagious source).  
• Otherwise not discussed.

Physical Examination:
(Not performed – remote consultation; no vitals provided.)

Investigations:
• Planned: Stool sample for culture/MC&S to rule out bacterial gastroenteritis.  
• Planned: Clinical hydration assessment at urgent clinic visit.  
(No results available.)

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Acute diarrhoea & vomiting – probable infectious gastroenteritis with dehydration risk.  
  • Arrange urgent clinic appointment for stool sample and hydration assessment.  
  • Continue oral rehydration solution: very small, frequent sips.  
  • Dietary advice: bland foods (toast, biscuits); avoid fruit, vegetables, milk.  
  • Monitor urine output; seek urgent care (A&E) if unable to keep fluids down, reduced urine output, worsening symptoms, or red-flag signs (blood in stool, severe pain, persistent fever).  
  • Provide contact number for support line; patient to call if deterioration.

Issue 2: Potential dehydration.  
  • Reinforce importance of fluid intake as above.  
  • Check vitals and consider IV fluids at clinic/A&E if signs of dehydration.

General plan items:  
  • Book urgent Babylon clinic appointment via support line as agreed.  
  • Safety-netting: attend A&E if condition worsens before scheduled review.

Quality checks (document_quality):
• Missing expected elements: Drug/food allergies not elicited; complete medication list and doses not documented; no objective vitals.  
• Internal conflicts: None noted.  
• Transcript quality: Clear; occasional minor inaudible blanks but clinically adequate.
